To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the data management of real-time sensor data is a challenging task that can be supported with a variety of technologies.

real-time sensor data stream management is an emerging area that is currently receiving a lot of attention from the research community, and that there is a wide range of data management technologies that can be used for analyzing real-time sensor streams.

the data management technologies for real-time sensor data stream processing can be categorized into four categories based on the data processing model, namely the stream processing model, the window processing model, the sliding-window processing model, and the continuous query processing model, and that each data management technology has its own advantages and disadvantages in terms of the performance of real-time sensor data processing, the complexity of real-time sensor query processing, and the scalability of real-time sensor stream processing.

the following challenges: (i) How to store and index the sensor data streams? (ii) How to efficiently retrieve the sensor data streams from the storage? (iii) How to efficiently query the sensor data streams on the server? (iv) How to efficiently analyze the sensor data streams at the client?

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no single best data management technology for all real-time data stream applications, but rather that the best technology depends on the application domain.
the current state of the art in real-time data stream management systems is still in its infancy and that there is a lot of room for improvement in the area of real-time data stream processing.
the data management community has made a significant step in the direction of managing and analyzing massive streams of real-time sensor data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a data management framework for geosensor networks that allows for real-time analysis of sensor data streams.
we have developed a new data stream management system called STREAM that is capable of handling large numbers of real-time sensor streams in real-time.
we have developed a new approach for managing and analyzing massive real-time sensor data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the data management community should develop new data management techniques that are specifically tailored for managing real-time sensor data.
the traditional database technologies are not sufficient to handle the massive real-time data.
the data management community needs to develop new technologies for processing real-time sensor data in order to support the next generation of geosensor applications.
